# What is my job?

::: {.small}
> Most professors were often deeply antagonistic toward, even scornful of,
any approach to learning emerging from a philosophical standpaint emphasizing
the union of mind, body, and spirit, rather than the separation of these 
elements. Like many of the students I now teach, I was often told by powerful
academics that I was misguided to seek such a perspective in the academy.
Throughout my student years I felt deep inner anguish. Memory of that pain
returns as I listen to students express the concern that they will not succeed
in academic professions if they want to be well, if they eschew dysfunctional
behavior or participation in coercive hierarchies. These students are often
fearful, as I was, that there are no spaces in the academy where the will to be
self-actualized can be affirmed.

bell hooks, *Teaching to Transgress*
:::

# Code Style

In general, we will use the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/)
for guidance on how to format our code. 

. . .

Good code formatting makes it easier for others to read your code! Since you
will be collaborating with others throughout the course, it is important to
write code that is easy to understand!

## Universal Principles

- Spaces before and after `=` (e.g., `mean = mean(x)`)
- Spaces after commas (e.g., `aes(x = hwy, y = cty)`)
- No line of code should be over 80 characters long.
    + If your line is longer than 80 characters, you should use new lines 
    (returns) to break up your code. 
    + The contents should be indented by two spaces.

::: {.callout-important}
# Let's demo how to get a line at 80 characters!
:::

## `ggplot` Code

It is good practice to put each `geom` and `aes` on a new line.

::: panel-tabset

### Bad

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: poorly-formatted-ggplot-code
#| code-line-numbers: false

ggplot(data = mpg, mapping = aes(x = cty, y = hwy, color = class)) + geom_point() + theme_bw() + labs(x = "City (mpg)", y = "Highway (mpg)")
```
:::

### Good

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: better-formatted-ggplot-code
#| code-line-numbers: false

ggplot(data = mpg, 
       mapping = aes(x = cty, y = hwy, color = class)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x = "City (mpg)", y = "Highway (mpg)")
```
:::
:::

## `dplyr` Code

It is good practice to have a new line after every pipe.

::: panel-tabset

### Bad

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: poorly-formatted-dplyr-code
#| code-line-numbers: false

mpg |>
  summarise(mean_hwy = mean(hwy), mean_cty = mean(cty), mean_displ = mean(displ), .by = manufacturer)

mpg |> summarize(across(where(is.numeric), mean), .by = manufacturer) |>
pivot_longer(!manufacturer, names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
arrange(value)
```
:::

### Good

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: better-formatted-dplyr-code
#| code-line-numbers: false

mpg |>
  summarise(
    mean_hwy = mean(hwy), 
    mean_cty = mean(cty), 
    mean_displ = mean(displ), 
    .by = manufacturer
    )

mpg |> 
  summarize(
    across(where(is.numeric), mean), .by = manufacturer
    ) |>
  pivot_longer(!manufacturer, names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") |>
  arrange(value)
```
:::
:::

## Why use the pipe?

The pipe is a powerful way to make your code more readable by passing the output
of one funtion as the input of the next function. 

**No more nested functions!**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: false

## Good
map(diamonds, summ_stats) |> 
  bind_rows(.id = "id")

## Bad
bind_rows(map(diamonds, summ_stats),
          .id = "id")
```

## Which pipe to use?

As of R 4.3.0, the base pipe (`|>`) provides all the features from magrittr 
(`%>%`) that we recommend using.

::: {.callout-important}
# Let's demo how to get the base pipe as the default!
:::

## Saving Intermediate Objects

Objects should only be saved if they are needed to be refereced later!

::: panel-tabset

### Bad

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: lots-of-objects
#| code-line-numbers: false
#| code-overflow: scroll

summ_stats <- function(x){
  if(is.numeric(x)){
    mean = mean(x)
    median = median(x)
    sd = sd(x)
    iqr = IQR(x)
    summary <- tibble(Mean = mean, 
                      Median = median,
                      SD = sd,
                      IQR = iqr)
    return(summary)
  } else if (is.factor(x) || is.character(x)) {
    num_levels = n_distinct(x)
    summary <- tibble(`Number of Levels` = num_levels)
    return(summary)
  } else {
    warning("Unsupported input type")
    return(NULL)
  }
}
```
:::

### Good

::: {.small}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| label: no-objects
#| code-line-numbers: false
#| code-overflow: scroll

summ_df <- function(dataframe){
  if(is.data.frame(dataframe)){
    
    dataframe |>
      map(summ_stats) |>
      bind_rows(.id = "variable") |>
      pivot_longer(
        cols = -variable,
        names_to = "statistic",
        values_to = "value") |>
      pivot_wider(
        names_from = variable,
        values_from = value)
    
  } else {
    warning("Input is not a dataframe")
  }
}

```
:::
:::
